chunks: Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir narrated from Abū al-Ṣaḥārī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A man bought a house, and an empty plot remained, so he built on it a revenue-generating house. Should he endow it for the mosque?
He said: Indeed, the Magians endowed property for the fire temple.

key_terms.الْمَجُوسَ: the Magians, mentioned here as an example of people making religious endowments
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque as the beneficiary of the endowment
key_terms.بَيْتَ غَلَّةٍ: a building intended to produce income or yield revenue
key_terms.عَرْصَةٌ: an open plot or vacant piece of land
key_terms.يُوقِفُهُ: to dedicate it as an endowment

ai.seo_question: Can a revenue-generating property be endowed for a mosque in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the permissibility and precedent of dedicating income-producing property as a waqf for a mosque. The Imam عليه السلام answers by citing that even the Magians endowed property for their places of worship, indicating the recognized practice of endowment for religious institutions.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5594 - Al-Abbas ibn Amir narrated from Abu Al-Sahari, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
I asked Imam (as) about a man who bought a house, and there remained an empty plot of land. He built upon it a house to generate income. Should he endow it for the mosque?
Imam (as) replied: "Indeed, the Magians endowed property for their fire temples."
